operations.summary: List redacted immutable notification delivery facts
operations.description: Platform administrators with system_configuration.read or platform.admin may query all scopes or one exact scope. Session, membership and current permissions are revalidated before query validation and lookup. One row identifies one immutable outbox sequence, including anonymous recipients and replay generations. Filters combine with AND. Without from/to the complete history is queried. Each optional bound is inclusive; when both are supplied, to must be greater than from and the window at most 31 days. The current request uses one consistent database view for cursor validation, total_count and rows. Pages are ordered by observed_at, outbox_id and sequence descending. Cursors identify persisted facts and are validated against the current filters; they do not promise a snapshot across requests. Delivery history never includes message titles, bodies, full recipient contacts, provider response bodies, deduplication keys, lease tokens or credentials. New transport calls record only a masked recipient address and provider_call_started_at. A row sees only an observation in the same attempt through its own sequence; dispatch_started never reads a future settlement observation. Historical rows without observations remain null and are never backfilled from current user contacts. Message content retains its separate administrator message-query contract.

params.name: scope_id
params.description: Optional exact scope; omitted means all scopes for an authorized platform administrator.

params.name: state
params.type: string: pending / dispatching / retry_wait / accepted / unknown / delivered / permanent_failed / exhausted / cancelled

params.name: result
params.description: success means only delivered; failure means retry_wait, permanent_failed or exhausted. accepted, unknown, lease_unknown and cancelled are neither success nor failure. When state is also supplied, both filters must match; a contradiction returns an empty page.

params.name: event_type
params.description: Exact persisted notification event type, not a legacy UI alias.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Canonical lowercase nonzero UUID or positive decimal display ID, at most signed int64 maximum; filters recipients, not actors.

params.name: message_id
params.description: Exact immutable notification_events.id, shared by original and replay outboxes.

params.name: from
params.description: Inclusive observed_at lower bound, RFC3339 with optional fractional seconds.

params.name: to
params.description: Inclusive observed_at upper bound, RFC3339 with optional fractional seconds.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Returned outbox UUID and positive int32 fact sequence; must identify a fact satisfying the current filters.

operations.description: Event-centric administrator view of member notification facts. Fields that are not backed by durable facts are returned as null. Site and package use the subject recorded when the event was raised; older package-monitor rows fall back to the monitor transition's exact subscription. Events raised without a site subject never match a site filter, and ownership is never inferred from current bindings. Titles, channel bodies and email_state/sms_state come from original generation-1 outbox facts (null = that channel was not generated); delivery replay does not duplicate message rows.

params.name: package_id
params.description: Exact user subscription ID from a monitor transition; product IDs do not match. Unknown IDs return an empty page.

params.name: site_id
params.description: Site recorded when the event was raised (notification_events.subject_site_id); events without a site subject never match.

params.name: user
params.description: Recipient user by exact display ID or case-insensitive substring of username / display name (current values).

params.name: package
params.description: User subscription by exact display ID or case-insensitive substring of the package name; events whose subscription no longer exists never match.

params.name: site
params.description: Event-time site by exact display ID or case-insensitive substring of its current domain; events whose site no longer exists never match.
